Heard Sri Rajeev Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner, Shri Fuzail Ahmad Ansari, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State respondents and Shri Kuldeep Singh Chauhan,
Dilip Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57519766/
2 learned counsel appearing for the Authority and Sri Gaurang Tiwari, holding brief of Sri Tejasvi Misra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Authority in connected petition.
2. With the consent of both the parties, both the writ petitions are being decided by this common judgment.
3. Both the writ petitions are being preferred praying inter alia for the following relief :-
" Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the Respondent No.2 to consider the application of the petitioner dated 12.06.2025 for sanction of map for construction on Gata No. 550 Village Kirra, Pargana Khurja, District Bulandshahr within such period as may be prescribed by this Hon'ble High Court.

sentences.text:
"
AND "(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents not to acquire/take possession of Plot No. 550 situated at Gram Kirra, Pargana Khurja, District Bulandshahr from the petitioner.

(ii) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to pay such heavy compensation to the petitioner for the illegal and unauthorized demolition of his Plot No. 550 situated at Gram Kirra, Pargana Khurja, District Bulandshahr."
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in Writ C No.13013 of 2015, the co-ordinate Bench of this Court passed the following order :-
" 1.

Having regard to the submissions made and the averments in the writ petition,
we require Vice Chairman, Bulandshahr, Khurja Development Authority to file his affidavit and disclose the basis on which demolition, if any, has been carried out and in that event also disclose the procedure, which was followed.

2. List in 2nd week of July, 2025.
3.

Learned counsel for the respondent, Development Authority, states that the Development Authority does not intend to dispossess the petitioner and therefore, we are not passing any order of interim protection in favour of the petitioner in this regard.

"
5. Subsequently, Writ C No.37471 of 2025 has been preferred for commanding the Respondent No.2 to consider the application of the petitioner dated 12.06.2025 for sanction of map for construction over Gata No. 550 Village Kirra, Pargana Khurja, District Bulandshahr.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that admittedly, the land in question has not been acquired by the Development Authority.
As the boundary wall was removed, the petitioner had initially preferred the aforementioned proceeding, wherein the respondent had assured that they are not intending to dispossess the petitioner.

He next submits that in absence of any such acquisition Dilip Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57519766/
3 or through agreement, the petitioner may not be dispossessed from his holding except in accordance with law.

sentences.text: He further submits that in case, the respondents are not inclined to utilize the land for some development plan, in such situation, for indefinite period they may not be permitted not to process the application of the petitioner for sanction of map duly moved under section 14/15 of the U.P. Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973 (the Act, 1973).

entities.text: U.P. Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that as the respondents have not taken any such steps either to acquire the land or to negotiate with the tenure-holder to purchase the land with agreeable rate till date, a direction be issued to the respondents to sanction the map.
7. Considering the factual situation, we are not inclined to keep both the petitions pending consideration.

Suffice it to indicate that in case, the respondent - Development Authority is not inclined to acquire the land for development plan, in such situation, it is always open to the Authority to take recourse as available under the law.
For indefinite period, the application of the petitioner for sanction of may cannot be held in limbo.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, both the writ petitions stand disposed of with an observation that in case, the Authority is inclined to acquire the land, the same is to be carried out strictly in accordance with law and in case, there is no development plan to be carried out as per their initial inclination which is reflected from the stand taken by the Development Authority, we find that the application of the petitioner for sanction of map is to be considered in accordance with law.
9. With the aforesaid observations, both the writ petitions stand disposed of.
